claims.title: Mature urban phase of the Indus cities
claims.summary: Harappa, Mohenjo-daro and hundreds of other settlements reach their peak, with grid-planned streets, advanced drainage and standardised weights across a vast trading network.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-2600bce-mature-urban-phase-of-the-indus-cities, claim TL:IND:event:2600bce:mature-urban-phase-of-the-indus-cities, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mohenjo-daro flourishes
claims.summary: Mohenjo-daro, on the Indus in modern Pakistan, becomes one of the civilisation's largest cities and is today a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its Great Bath and citadel.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-2600bce-mohenjo-daro-flourishes, claim TL:IND:event:2600bce:mohenjo-daro-flourishes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Decline of the Harappan cities
claims.summary: The major cities are gradually abandoned as weakening monsoons and shifting rivers undermine the agricultural base, marking the end of the civilisation's urban phase.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-1900bce-decline-of-the-harappan-cities, claim TL:IND:event:1900bce:decline-of-the-harappan-cities, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Composition of the Rigveda
claims.summary: The Rigveda, the oldest Vedic text and a foundational scripture of Hinduism, is composed in early Sanskrit and preserved through oral tradition.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-1500bce-composition-of-the-rigveda, claim TL:IND:event:1500bce:composition-of-the-rigveda, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Buddha and Mahavira
claims.summary: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha) founds Buddhism and Mahavira reforms Jainism, launching two enduring religions amid a wider questioning of Vedic ritual.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-500bce-rise-of-the-buddha-and-mahavira, claim TL:IND:event:500bce:rise-of-the-buddha-and-mahavira, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Chandragupta Maurya founds the Maurya Empire
claims.summary: Chandragupta Maurya overthrows the Nanda dynasty and builds the first empire to unify most of the subcontinent, with its capital at Pataliputra.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-322bce-chandragupta-maurya-founds-the-maurya-empire, claim TL:IND:event:322bce:chandragupta-maurya-founds-the-maurya-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ashoka's conquest of Kalinga and conversion
claims.summary: After the devastating Kalinga war, Emperor Ashoka embraces Buddhism, renounces conquest, and spreads an ethic of dharma through inscribed edicts across his vast empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-261bce-ashoka-s-conquest-of-kalinga-and-conversion, claim TL:IND:event:261bce:ashoka-s-conquest-of-kalinga-and-conversion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Gupta golden age
claims.summary: The Gupta Empire presides over a classical flowering of Sanskrit literature, mathematics and astronomy, including the works of Kalidasa and Aryabhata and the maturing of the decimal system.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-320-gupta-golden-age, claim TL:IND:event:320:gupta-golden-age, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Delhi Sultanate
claims.summary: Qutb al-Din Aibak establishes independent rule at Delhi, beginning a 320-year succession of Islamic dynasties that reshape the politics and culture of northern India.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-1206-founding-of-the-delhi-sultanate, claim TL:IND:event:1206:founding-of-the-delhi-sultanate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Babur founds the Mughal Empire
claims.summary: Babur defeats Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat, ending the Delhi Sultanate and establishing the Mughal Empire, which would rule much of the subcontinent for over two centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-1526-babur-founds-the-mughal-empire, claim TL:IND:event:1526:babur-founds-the-mughal-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Akbar
claims.summary: Akbar the Great consolidates and expands the empire, reforms its administration with the mansabdari system, and pursues a policy of religious tolerance and cultural synthesis.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-1556-reign-of-akbar, claim TL:IND:event:1556:reign-of-akbar, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Aurangzeb and Mughal decline
claims.summary: Aurangzeb dies after extending the empire to its greatest extent; his costly wars and religious policies leave the Mughal state weakened, and its authority rapidly fragments thereafter.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-1707-death-of-aurangzeb-and-mughal-decline, claim TL:IND:event:1707:death-of-aurangzeb-and-mughal-decline, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Plassey
claims.summary: Robert Clive's East India Company forces defeat the Nawab of Bengal, marking the beginning of British political and military dominance in India.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-1757-battle-of-plassey, claim TL:IND:event:1757:battle-of-plassey, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British Crown rule begins
claims.summary: After the suppression of the 1857 rebellion, the Crown abolishes East India Company rule and assumes direct governance of India, beginning the British Raj.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-1858-british-crown-rule-begins, claim TL:IND:event:1858:british-crown-rule-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Salt March
claims.summary: Gandhi leads a 24-day march to the sea to make salt in defiance of the British salt monopoly, galvanising mass non-violent resistance against colonial rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-1930-the-salt-march, claim TL:IND:event:1930:the-salt-march, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bengal famine
claims.summary: An estimated two to three million people die in Bengal in a man-made famine driven by wartime inflation, export priorities and colonial policy rather than any major shortfall in food production.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-1943-bengal-famine, claim TL:IND:event:1943:bengal-famine, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence and Partition
claims.summary: India becomes independent from Britain under Prime Minister Nehru as the subcontinent is partitioned into India and Pakistan, unleashing mass migration and communal violence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-1947-independence-and-partition, claim TL:IND:event:1947:independence-and-partition, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Partition violence and mass migration
claims.summary: Up to 12–20 million people are uprooted and an estimated one to two million die in massacres and forced migration along the new India–Pakistan border.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of India: From the planned cities of the Indus to the world's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IND/chronicle#ev-1947-partition-violence-and-mass-migration, claim TL:IND:event:1947:partition-violence-and-mass-migration, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Constitution and the Republic
claims.summary: The Constitution of India comes into force, making India a sovereign democratic republic with universal suffrage and fundamental rights; the day is celebrated as Republic Day.
